lessons.title: Single Stroke Roll
lessons.description: Sixteenth notes, one stroke per hand in turn: R L R L. The foundation of every roll and most fills.
tips: Start each stroke from the same height so both hands sound alike.
Let the stick bounce back up on its own; lift, don't press.
Speed comes last: keep it even at a slow tempo before raising it.

lessons.title: Single Stroke Four
lessons.description: A 4-stroke phrase of alternating single strokes, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Single Stroke Seven

lessons.title: Multiple Bounce Roll
lessons.description: A buzz roll: each hand presses the stick into the head so it bounces several times, and the hands alternate on every eighth note.
tips: Keep a little pressure in the fingers so each stroke buzzes rather than bounces twice.
Aim for one smooth, continuous sound with no gaps where the hands change.
Keep both hands' buzzes the same length and volume.

lessons.title: Triple Stroke Roll
lessons.description: Groups of three strokes per hand, alternating right and left, with a short rest between groups.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Double Stroke Open Roll
lessons.description: Two strokes per hand, R R L L. Each slashed eighth note is played as two sixteenths with the same hand.
tips: Make the second stroke of each pair as loud as the first.
At slow tempos play both strokes from the wrist; let the fingers take over as it speeds up.
Listen for a steady stream of notes, not pairs.

lessons.title: Single Paradiddle
lessons.description: Two single strokes and a double, R L R R, then the same starting on the left, L R L L. The first note of each group is accented.
tips: Play the accent from a higher stick and the other notes low.
The double at the end of each group sets up the other hand's accent; keep it relaxed.
Say it as you play: pa-ra-did-dle.

lessons.title: Flam
lessons.description: A quiet grace note just before an accented main note, alternating hands: the grace note is played by the other hand.
tips: Hold the grace-note stick low and the main stick high, so both land almost together.
Aim for one thick sound, not two separate hits.
After each flam, the hand that played the main note drops low for the next grace note.

lessons.title: Flam Accent
lessons.description: Triplets with an accented flam on the first note of each beat, followed by two quiet taps. The lead hand changes every beat.
tips: Count it in threes: flam, tap, tap.
Keep the two taps low and even, so the accented flam stands out.
The last tap of each group is the next flam's grace note hand; let it stay low.

lessons.title: Drag
lessons.description: Two quick grace notes from one hand, played as a soft double stroke, lead into an accented note from the other hand.
tips: Play the two grace notes low and close together, like a small bounce.
Keep them quieter than the main note, which is accented.
Practice the grace notes alone first: a soft, even double stroke.
